newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Dragonair seeks two new Japanese routes.
newsitem.headline: Dragonair seeks two new Japanese routes.

text.p: Hong Kong Dragon Airlines Limited (Dragonair) is in negotiations with the Japanese government for approval to start new services to Niigata and Komatsu, the airline's newly appointed chief executive Stanley Hui told Reuters.

"We've been talking for quite a while now and I certainly hope we get some solutions by the end of the year. There is proven market potential to both those destinations. We've regularly flown charters there and they've proven to be quite popular," Hui said in an interview.

Hong Kong's expanding regional carrier said the Japanese market is of increasing importance. Dragonair currently flies to Hiroshima and Sendai six times a week with Airbus A320 aircraft which typically seats 150 passengers. Hui said his aim is to upgrade the service to larger Airbus A330 aircraft with around 255 seats in the second half of this year.

Industry sources said all the Hong Kong-based airlines - Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd,, all-cargo airline AHK Air Hong Kong Ltd and Dragonair - are increasing services to Japan, regarded as a highly profitable market place for both passengers and cargo.

China National Aviation Corp holds some 36 percent of Dragonair, CITIC Pacific Ltd 28 percent, with Swire Pacific Ltd and Cathay Pacific jointly holding a further 26 percent. --Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542-7706 Fax+5017
